reader.title: Lynching of Nicholas Puct
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: The only report says Nicholas Puct was hanged by 'lynchers' on a grapevine (A1).
A1 says Puct was hanged by 'lynchers', which implies an extralegal killing by more than one person, but it gives no number, accusation or other details, and the line is partly unreadable OCR.
One wire roundup printed in one Washington paper (A1) is the only report found; no Texas paper or second account turned up.

summary.text: The lynching of Nicholas Puct was the hanging of a man by unnamed lynchers on a grapevine in Texas in December 1881.
It is known from a single line in a wire roundup of seven killings in the Texas border country, which gave no place, accusation or race for the victim.
The report appeared in a dispatch whose dateline appears to read Brownsville, Texas, collecting a day's violent deaths along the lower Rio Grande.

Its other items told of a man shot through the heart by an unknown assailant at Laredo, a fatal quarrel over a game of cards, an unknown Mexican "round murdered on a rami near Itlo Ornnda City," said to be the seventh Mexican killed there in six weeks, and two men found or reported murdered on the roads.
According to the dispatch, Puct "wus hung by lynchers ion grnpo vine estenlay," that is, hanged by lynchers on a grapevine the day before.
A run of unreadable words follows his name in the scanned text and may have described him or the circumstances, but nothing about an accusation, the size of the group or the place survives.

The dispatch is dated December 10 as the scan reads it, which would place the hanging on December 9, but the roundup was headed "Sunday in Texas" and printed on Monday, December 19, so the date may have been misread.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.
The only copy found ran on the front page of the Washington Evening Critic on December 19, 1881, under the heading "SUNDAY IN TEXAS" and a subhead counting seven bloody deeds in a day.
The item was printed without comment as one entry in a list of border shootings, robberies and murders, and it said nothing about the victim's race.
No other version of the report, from a Texas paper or elsewhere, appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Wire roundup
accounts.gist: A dispatch from Texas, dateline apparently Brownsville, listed among seven killings that Nicholas Puct had been hung by lynchers on a grapevine the day before.

framing.detail: Printed under 'SUNDAY IN TEXAS' with a subhead roughly 'Seven [Deeds] of Blood Yesterday', with no comment, as one of a string of border killings.

record_check.dossier: Unclear is right: no race is given; the roundup's other victims are mostly Mexican or unidentified border men, so there is no sign this was an anti-Black killing
Follows the OCR dateline 'Dec 10'; the 'Sunday in Texas' heading and Dec 19 printing suggest the dateline may really be Dec 18, which would put the hanging about Dec 17
The item names no place; the roundup's dateline appears to be Brownsville, Texas, which is not necessarily where the hanging happened
